record.paper_title: Open Problems for Entire Functions of Bounded Index in Direction
record.original_question: Let L be a positive continuous function on C^n. For a nonzero direction c in C^n, say that an entire function H has bounded L-index in direction c if there is an integer m0 such that, for every point z and every m >= 0, |D_c^m H(z)|/(m! L(z)^m) is at most the maximum of |D_c^k H(z)|/(k! L(z)^k) over 0 <= k <= m0, where D_c is the directional derivative in direction c. Suppose f1 and f2 are entire functions of bounded L-index in the corresponding directions b1 and b2, and h is entire. For the first-order partial differential equation f1(z) D_b1 F(z) + f2(z) D_b2 F(z) = h(z), what direction b and what additional conditions on the data ensure that an entire solution F has bounded L-index in direction b?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $L:\mathbb{C}^n\to(0,\infty)$ be a positive continuous function, and for a nonzero direction $c\in\mathbb{C}^n$ let $D_c$ denote the directional derivative $D_c H(z)=\sum_{j=1}^n c_j\,\partial H/\partial z_j$, with iterates $D_c^m$. An entire function $H:\mathbb{C}^n\to\mathbb{C}$ is said to have bounded $L$-index in the direction $c$ if there exists a nonnegative integer $m_0$ such that, for every $z\in\mathbb{C}^n$ and every integer $m\ge 0$,
$$\frac{|D_c^m H(z)|}{m!\,L(z)^m}\;\le\;\max_{0\le k\le m_0}\frac{|D_c^k H(z)|}{k!\,L(z)^k}.$$
Let $b_1,b_2\in\mathbb{C}^n\setminus\{0\}$ be two directions, and let $f_1,f_2,h:\mathbb{C}^n\to\mathbb{C}$ be entire functions such that $f_1$ has bounded $L$-index in the direction $b_1$ and $f_2$ has bounded $L$-index in the direction $b_2$. Consider the first-order linear partial differential equation
$$f_1(z)\,D_{b_1}F(z)+f_2(z)\,D_{b_2}F(z)=h(z).$$
Determine a direction $b\in\mathbb{C}^n\setminus\{0\}$ and additional hypotheses on the data $f_1,f_2,h,b_1,b_2,L$ that guarantee every entire solution $F$ of this equation has bounded $L$-index in the direction $b$.
artifact.category_tag: Entire functions of bounded L-index in direction
artifact.status_search_result: Related results exist for second-order linear PDEs and higher-order directional differential equations with bounded L-index hypotheses (e.g., works on slice holomorphic solutions and entire solutions of linear PDEs), but no source found directly resolves the stated first-order two-direction problem with general data $f_1,f_2,h$. Status appears unresolved in full generality based on available search results.

status_evidence.title: Boundedness of the L-index in a direction of entire solutions of second order partial differential equation
status_evidence.snippet: Sufficient conditions for boundedness of L-index in a direction for entire solutions of certain second-order linear PDEs.
status_evidence.claim: Related but addresses second-order equations, not the stated first-order two-direction equation.

status_evidence.title: Slice holomorphic solutions of some directional differential equations with bounded L-index in the same direction
status_evidence.snippet: Studies slice holomorphic solutions of directional differential equations of bounded L-index in the same direction.
status_evidence.claim: Treats single-direction equations; does not address the mixed two-direction first-order equation as posed.

status_evidence.title: Properties of entire solutions of some linear PDE's
status_evidence.snippet: Properties of entire solutions of linear PDEs with bounded index conditions.
status_evidence.claim: General context but no direct resolution of the posed problem.
